failures.criterion: The merge gate: the head the reviewer approves must be one whose checks ran. The repository's own rule is that a push carrying code takes no `skip-checks: true` trailer, and that a wrong trailer stalls the issue and never passes it.
failures.evidence:
No CI ran on any commit of round 5. `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq .total_count` answers 0 for the code commit 4ceb9de44891 and 0 for the pull request's head 45472f8b629e; `gh run list --repo sjawhar/legion --branch legion/INFRA-484` shows no run at either sha. The cause is in the push: its head 45472f8b ends with `skip-checks: true` while the same push carried the code commit 4ceb9de44891 (123 files from the fork point e9398987d010, 8689 insertions across the branch), so GitHub started no run for any of it.

This is the second time. Round 2 was pushed the same way (code under a trailered head, CI run 40989912519 cancelled and nothing started), the architect told the implementer afterwards, and round 4 was pushed correctly — the code commit a62d9ba7be6b untrailered, so run 41019320047 started on it, and the handoff trailered.

The consequence is not cosmetic. The daemon classifies a push by the paths its commits touch and never by the trailer, so the push carrying 4ceb9de44891 is a code push whose verdict never arrives; the reviewer reads CI at the head it approves and finds none; and a base that requires a check will not merge a head whose checks never ran, so the merge waits and the daemon tells the architect after an hour.

I cannot fix it from here. My own push this round is handoff-only — I found no defect to pin with a red test — so it takes the trailer and starts no run. The remedy is one push by the implementer whose head carries no trailer, after which CI runs on a head containing the round-5 code. Everything else I could run is green, so the round after that is short.
